title: Honors: Who's Who, key to New Orleans and the Mood Indigo Hall of Fame
summary: Mrs. Bigard lists his Who's Who entry since 1949, the 1972 New Orleans key to the city from Mayor Landrieu and a plaque, and the Hall of Fame award for songwriting 'Mood Indigo'.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: In the home of Barney and Dorothee Bigard there are some very interesting awards, trophies, plaques, showing some marvelous honors for a long career, and Mrs. Dorothee Bigard has made a list of all of them. We haven't really had a chance to discuss all of them, so I'm going to give the microphone to Mrs. Bigard right now and she and Barney will talk.

Thank you, Pat. Oh, I just wanted to be sure that a note was made on Barney's achievements which are well deserved and should be recognized, and that he was listed in Who's Who in America and has been since 1949, and his -- At the New Orleans Jazzfest in 1972, he was given the key to the city by the mayor of New Orleans, Mayor Landrieu, and also Achievement of Merit -- Merit of Achievement, rather, a plaque which is a beautiful honor for

Barney and well deserved. And he also has received an award for the Hall of Fame from the National Academy of Recording Artists and Sciences for being the songwriter, namely Barney Bigard, of 'Mood Indigo.' [and Grammy Award].
Would you like to say something about that, Honey?
That merit thing from New Orleans was really a gasser, --

-- especially that key. You know, that key is so large. It's about as big as a gnat's ass, and I enjoyed it, so I got it -- it's a specialty in my den. And I like for everybody that comes around and visits me to see it. I make it a point that they see that key, it's such a beauty. But all in all it's really beautiful. I like it very much. I enjoyed every bit of it. And then, the rest of it, why, --
